strengths: Novel and well-motivated central question — challenging the common intuition that depth alone drives MIA resistance in collaborative inference, supported by concrete empirical counterexamples on ViT, ResNet, and IR-152 before the theoretical analysis is even introduced.

Rigorous information-theoretic derivation (entropy upper bounds via maximum-entropy Gaussian and determinant-trace inequality, full proofs in Appendix A) linking the H(X|Z) lower bound to an interpretable quantity R²_c, and an honest treatment of the differential-to-discrete entropy bridge under finite precision (Appendix B-C), including explicit acknowledgment that the correction term κ_Δ(m) can be loose.

Extensive empirical validation spanning four architectures (IR-152, ResNet-50, VGG19, ViT) and multiple datasets (CIFAR-10, FaceScrub, KMNIST/MNIST/EMNIST), with consistent findings that dimension-matched deeper layers do not guarantee resistance, supporting the representational-transition thesis.

Practical contributions beyond pure theory: an automatic GPZ-locating algorithm (Algorithm 1) with dimension normalization and stability checks (across sampling seeds, training seeds, and LS condition), plus a thorough deployment-overhead analysis (latency, communication, memory, energy) that connects the theoretical findings to real deployment tradeoffs.

Multiple stress tests of the core claim: entropy-enhancement ablations (FFT, normalization, NN-based) and inversion-model-enhancement ablations (attention variants) both show decision-level representations remain comparatively robust, strengthening the causal story rather than relying on a single fixed attacker.
Code availability is mentioned (GitHub links for model/training and inversion architecture), aiding reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central theoretical bound is explicitly acknowledged to be potentially 'numerically loose' and can become 'vacuous in absolute value' once the finite-precision correction κ_Δ(m) is included; the qualitative ordering argument (via data-processing inequality) partially compensates, but this materially weakens claims that the bound is directly actionable rather than a coarse indicator.

The 'Neural Vortex' concept, presented as a headline contribution in the abstract/intro, is explicitly downgraded in the appendix (Sec. G) to 'only an intuitive interpretation... not a standalone formal mechanism,' which creates a tension between how prominently it is marketed in the main text versus its actual epistemic status.

No direct quantitative comparison against existing published defenses (noise injection, information bottleneck methods, PATROL, PrivaScissors, etc.) is provided; the paper explicitly frames this as out of scope ('the appropriate evaluation is theory validity... rather than head-to-head comparison'), but this makes it hard for readers to judge how GPZ-based partitioning compares to the privacy-utility tradeoffs of prior defenses it critiques.

The active-location algorithm is validated on only two architectures (IR-152, VGG19) in Table 5, and the claimed post-hoc/active duality is somewhat circular—MIA outcomes are still needed to confirm the located zone is correct, softening the 'deployment-oriented guidance' claim.

Scope is restricted to vision/CNN and one small ViT configuration; the extension to Transformers/text is explicitly left as a 'cautious hypothesis' for future work, limiting the generality of the findings despite claims of broad applicability implied by 'collaborative inference' framing.

Reported aggregate numbers (4× MSE increase, 66% stronger resistance) are averages over multiple settings without variance/confidence intervals in the main text, and the extensive appendix tables (though detailed) are not accompanied by statistical significance testing across repeated runs for the headline results.

The overall presentation is extremely dense, with substantial reliance on ~37 pages of appendix for core proofs and even for some central experimental interpretation (e.g., R²_c evolution visualizations only qualitatively discussed via t-SNE in Fig. 3 without a quantitative trend plot in the main text).
